verdict.rationale: YYLO's own CLI accepts natural-language task prompts that it routes to coding agents, for example `yylo init --task "..."` and `yy pi '...'`. It also ships Skills described as procedures for operating YYLO and Ledger, which steer an agent. However, YYLO's own operations (ledger, task start, merge land) are driven by structured subcommands, not natural language. Missing for 10: documented natural-language control of YYLO's own commands (task, merge, ledger) rather than only prompts passed to subagents, and hands-on or independent corroboration of agent-driven operation via Skills.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: yylo init --task "Describe one verifiable outcome" --subagent claude
yy pi --no-session 'Summarize this repository. Do not edit files.'
YYLO Skills are independently versioned, reusable procedures for operating YYLO and Ledger.
A skill can steer an agent and may reference executable procedures.
